title: Finland – Air-charter services – Charter Flights – Small Business Aircraft 2027
description: This framework agreement covers the provision of charter flights for passengers with small business aircraft. Requirements for the framework agreement are outlined in the Call for Tenders and its appendices, in particular in Annex 1 "Subject-matter". Charter flight services shall fulfill the regulations of the European Union’s mandatory legislation and of mandatory Finnish laws and decrees as well as regulations issued by the Finnish authorities. The usage of the small business aircraft services in the framework agreement of Hansel during a four-year contract period of 2021-2025 was the following: - 103 charter flights with small business aircraft - one (1) ambulance and medical evacuation flight for one (1) patient - 80 % of the departures were from Helsinki-Vantaa Airport, 10 % of the departures were from other airports in Finland and 10 % of the departures were from abroad - destinations were mainly to Europe and Middle East - about 90 % of the flights were round-trip flights and about 10 % of the flights were one way flights. During the period from January 2026 to August 2026, the usage of the services was as follows: - A total of 12 flights were operated - All flights departed from Helsinki-Vantaa Airport - All destinations were located within Europe - Most flights were round trips, while a small number included multiple destinations - The average flight distance was 2,223 nautical miles, ranging from 1,266 to 3,190 nautical miles - The average number of passengers per flight was 9, with passenger loads ranging from 2 to 18. The information above is provided for indicative purposes only and is based on historical service usage. The figures are estimates only and do not constitute a commitment as to future flight volumes, passenger volumes, destinations, or procurement quantities. According to the customers, departures are going to be mainly from Helsinki-Vantaa Airport (EFHK) and Tampere-Pirkkala Airport (EFTP). Possible destinations for the forthcoming contract term are listed in the Annex A "Customers and Destinations". The estimated amount of flights per year for the forthcoming contract term is stated in the Annex A "Customers and Destinations". When taking into account the nature of the service, international circumstances are affecting for the need of the charter flight service. Therefore the actual usage of the framework agreement may differ from the previous framework agreement and the estimations of the customers. The subject of the framework agreement is described in more detail in the Call for Tenders and its annexes. CONTRACT TERM The term of the Agreement is one (1) year and nine (9) months. Hansel has the right to extend the contract term by a maximum of one option period of maximum one (1) year. Hansel will notify of the possible exercise or non-exercise of the option period no later than six (6) months before the end of the Agreement. Services based on the framework agreement can be provided during the term of the Agreement and service contracts. After the expiry, termination, or cancellation of the Agreement, new orders can no longer be made. All charter flights shall be flown within three (3) months period after the expiration of the Agreement. In addition, the contract term for the service contract may exceed three (3) months at the maximum the contract term of the Agreement. The terms and conditions of the Agreement shall be applied to such flights and service contracts even after the expiry of the Agreement. The start date referred to under section "duration" in the contract notice is an estimate of when the agreement will enter into force. THE SCOPE OF THE CALL FOR TENDERS Appendix A "Customers and destinations" of the Call for Tenders indicates the customers who are entitled to use the framework agreement, the possible destinations during the agreement term and the estimated number of flights per year. The estimated value during the contract term is 4 000 000 - 8 000 000 euros (VAT 0 %), including option period. The maximum value is therefore 8 000 000 euros (VAT 0 %). These figures are based on information provided by customers entitled to use the framework agreement and estimates made by Hansel. Framework agreement is covered by the Government Decree on Joint Procurement in Central Government (765/2006) and the Ministry of Finance Decision on Joint Procurement by the Central Government (766/2006). According to these regulations, government agencies and institutions of the state budget economy shall, in principle, use centrally procured contracts.

description: The consultant agreement shall cover the provision of technical services in support of DSA ́s core functions within regulatory work. The work shall include reviewing and assessing technical documentation and support for DSA in connection with inspections. There are three nuclear plants in Norway: the research reactor facilities in Kjeller and Halden, and the combined landfill and storage facility for low and medium radioactive waste in Himdalen. In 2018 the Norwegian government established a new government organisation, Norsk Nukleærdekommisjonering (NND), which will take over all Norwegian nuclear power plants in Kjeller, Halden and Himdalen from the original operator, Institute for Energy Engineering (IFE). NND will be responsible for the operation of the nuclear installations, the production of them and the handling of radioactive waste and used core fuel. So far the nuclear power plant in Halden has been transferred from IFE to NND, and the other two installations are close to being transferred. Before the shutdown can start, there are a number of processes that must be completed so that the operator(s) shall be able to make changes in the installations in a safe and responsible manner, and for the regulation authority (DSA) to be able to approve changes in accordance with regulations and international standards. In preparation for the liquidation and during the shutdown, there will be a need to establish a new waste handling facility, including plans for a US-developed mobile melt consolidation facility (MMC). The procurement is covered by the Security Act and reflected in the contracting authority ́s requirement specifications and security requirements. Tenderers who would like to offer in this procurement are asked separately to familiarise themselves with the stated guidelines, prerequisites and requirements.

title: Norway – Repair and maintenance services – Maintenance and further development of ServiceNow
description: Purpose Norsk Tipping (NT) currently uses ServiceNow, among other things, as IT Service Management and CSM tools and currently has a licence and maintenance agreement through DXC Technology. The contract expires in February 2027 and this procurement is a renewal of the maintenance contract for ServiceNow. NT is looking for a professional cooperation partner who can help maintain and further develop the current system. Tenderers must see possibilities, propose improvements and have good routines for development and support. The CSM module is used by Customer Service (Interactions/Case), Dealer service and some other small user groups (Case). Customer service is among norway's best and requires high efficiency in case handling with focus on quick access to information, getting pressure and high system degree. The system bears the mark that it has lived for almost 10 years. There are some technical debts that we need help cleaning up. Part of this is moving some internal APIs, which have been made available with MID-server, over to exposed facade services which are more responsive. The ITSM module is used to a very large degree by IT Operations, but also on customer service, dealer services (incident) and in Security. The case types in use are: incident, major incident, problem, change and request. NP's internal Service Desk and HR use Agent Workspace. ServiceDesk receives cases via the user portal, chat, telephone, attendance and e-mails that are automatically registered in ServiceNow. The case types they work with are primarily incident and request. It is a well developed Change management with a number of automated standard changes. ServiceNow is receiving more and more changes via pipeline or other integrations from internal Jira. The operational centre is the escalation point for general errors in the systems. They have monitoring and use, among other things, Splunk to receive events. Emphasis will be put on the tenderer ́s experience and competence in addition to operation and maintenance. Tenderers shall be a proactive consultant for the entire spectrum of services the contract covers. Whether there is new functionality in ServiceNow, a need for clearing in technical debts, smart choices around integrations, utilisation of functionality in the existing system based on the supplier knowing NP's business needs or the like. Requirements that shall be met. Norsk Tipping has organised development work in a product development model. The Customer Support product area is responsible for i.a. management and further development of ServiceNow, Genesys Cloud and self-service systems. Developers and consultants from the chosen supplier in this procurement will be important resources in this team together with other internal and external resources. NT has few, but good internal resources with competence in ServiceNow, and it is important to have a professional supplier that provides me good access to resources and who can contribute with expert help. As a starting point, the team consists of a system manager/owner and two system administrators, one of whom is defined as a team architect. The product development area currently consists of two multi-disciplinary teams, but which share internal resources and to a large degree work across. The product development manager has management responsibility for the teams and has, in addition, a team management role for the teams, in order to ensure progress and prioritising tasks. The product area is responsible for the management assignments being carried out and together prioritise small and large assignments based on the company principles for product development. The product development area follows the company ́s development cycle together with the other 12 areas and a joint plan is carried out at a general level, approx. 3 times per annum. The detailed planning will mainly be carried out in 2-week sprinters. Errors that occur are continually corrected as well as ongoing work in the other processes. The tenderer is expected to have competence in the following main areas. The list is not exhaustive: · ServiceNow platform · Licenses · Administration · Development · Integrations and integration security · Active and proactive consulting (ServiceNow and technology/architecture) · Coordination and planning · Work in multi-disciplinary teams · SLA and support Norsk Tipping currently has an agreement with DXC for ServiceNow. The agreement includes both consultancy services for the operation, management and further development of ServiceNow, as well as ServiceNow licences. The two parts of the existing agreement have different lengths. The agreement on consultancy services expires 27 February 2027, while the existing agreement on ServiceNow licences runs until February 2029. A new contract that will be signed as a result of this competition shall include both consultancy services and ServiceNow licences.

Tarjoajan tulee tarjota asiakkaalle työtoimintapaikan sisältäen soveltuvat työtehtävät, tarvittavan ohjauksen ja välineet sekä turvalliset työtilat. Arvioinnissa ratkaisevaa ei siten olisi, tuottaako työtoiminnan hyvinvointialue, yhdistys, säätiö vai yritys, vaan se, käytetäänkö työtoimintaa korvaamaan sellaista työtä tai palvelua, joka muutoin toteutettaisiin vastiketta vastaan. title: Finland – Air-charter services – Charter Flights – Small Business Aircraft 2027
description: This framework agreement covers the provision of charter flights for passengers with small business aircraft. Requirements for the framework agreement are outlined in the Call for Tenders and its appendices, in particular in Annex 1 "Subject-matter". Charter flight services shall fulfill the regulations of the European Union’s mandatory legislation and of mandatory Finnish laws and decrees as well as regulations issued by the Finnish authorities. The usage of the small business aircraft services in the framework agreement of Hansel during a four-year contract period of 2021-2025 was the following: - 103 charter flights with small business aircraft - one (1) ambulance and medical evacuation flight for one (1) patient - 80 % of the departures were from Helsinki-Vantaa Airport, 10 % of the departures were from other airports in Finland and 10 % of the departures were from abroad - destinations were mainly to Europe and Middle East - about 90 % of the flights were round-trip flights and about 10 % of the flights were one way flights. During the period from January 2026 to August 2026, the usage of the services was as follows: - A total of 12 flights were operated - All flights departed from Helsinki-Vantaa Airport - All destinations were located within Europe - Most flights were round trips, while a small number included multiple destinations - The average flight distance was 2,223 nautical miles, ranging from 1,266 to 3,190 nautical miles - The average number of passengers per flight was 9, with passenger loads ranging from 2 to 18. The information above is provided for indicative purposes only and is based on historical service usage. The figures are estimates only and do not constitute a commitment as to future flight volumes, passenger volumes, destinations, or procurement quantities. According to the customers, departures are going to be mainly from Helsinki-Vantaa Airport (EFHK) and Tampere-Pirkkala Airport (EFTP). Possible destinations for the forthcoming contract term are listed in the Annex A "Customers and Destinations". The estimated amount of flights per year for the forthcoming contract term is stated in the Annex A "Customers and Destinations". When taking into account the nature of the service, international circumstances are affecting for the need of the charter flight service. Therefore the actual usage of the framework agreement may differ from the previous framework agreement and the estimations of the customers. The subject of the framework agreement is described in more detail in the Call for Tenders and its annexes. CONTRACT TERM The term of the Agreement is one (1) year and nine (9) months. Hansel has the right to extend the contract term by a maximum of one option period of maximum one (1) year. Hansel will notify of the possible exercise or non-exercise of the option period no later than six (6) months before the end of the Agreement. Services based on the framework agreement can be provided during the term of the Agreement and service contracts. After the expiry, termination, or cancellation of the Agreement, new orders can no longer be made. All charter flights shall be flown within three (3) months period after the expiration of the Agreement. In addition, the contract term for the service contract may exceed three (3) months at the maximum the contract term of the Agreement. The terms and conditions of the Agreement shall be applied to such flights and service contracts even after the expiry of the Agreement. The start date referred to under section "duration" in the contract notice is an estimate of when the agreement will enter into force. THE SCOPE OF THE CALL FOR TENDERS Appendix A "Customers and destinations" of the Call for Tenders indicates the customers who are entitled to use the framework agreement, the possible destinations during the agreement term and the estimated number of flights per year. The estimated value during the contract term is 4 000 000 - 8 000 000 euros (VAT 0 %), including option period. The maximum value is therefore 8 000 000 euros (VAT 0 %). These figures are based on information provided by customers entitled to use the framework agreement and estimates made by Hansel. Framework agreement is covered by the Government Decree on Joint Procurement in Central Government (765/2006) and the Ministry of Finance Decision on Joint Procurement by the Central Government (766/2006). title: Lowell Creek Tunnel Repairs, Seward, Alaska
description: THIS IS A PRESOLICITATION NOTICE ONLY FOR LOWELL CREEK TUNNEL REPAIRS, SEWARD, AK. OFFER OR BIDS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED FOR THIS NOTICE. This solicitation will be a full and open Invitation for Bid (IFB) with Definitive Responsibility Criteria. Any resulting contract will be firm-fixed priced. The solicitation for this project will be available by INTERNET ACCESS ONLY and the anticipated download availability date for this solicitation will be on or after 3 November 2026. Access to the documents will be through a link on the SAM.gov website: http://www.SAM.gov/. Use the Search function and use this solicitation number to Search by Solicitation/Award Number. Any future amendments to the solicitation will also be available for download from the SAM.gov website. The Contractor shall comply with commercial and industry standards as well as all applicable Federal, State, and local laws, regulations, and procedures. The Construction Wage Rates (formerly Davis-Bacon Act) will apply. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code will be 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction, which has a size standard of $45 Million. The total estimated magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. The type of contract shall be firm-fixed price. The estimated award date of this contract is December 2026 with a 1000 calendar-day period of performance. This project is contingent on availability of funds. If the project is cancelled, all bid preparation costs will be borne by the offeror. All offerors are advised that they must be registered in SAM.gov (http://www.SAM.gov/) when submitting a bid and at time of award. Joint ventures must also be registered in SAM.gov as a joint venture. Offerors who are not registered in SAM.gov should consider applying for registration immediately. Visit https://sam.gov/entity-registration for information on registration. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: Perform repairs of worn areas and install new center rails of the Lowell Creek Tunnel which is an approximately 2,100 feet long tunnel through Bear Mountain on the southwest side of Seward, Alaska. The tunnel is 10-foot high, horseshoe shaped tunnel which diverts Lowell Creek away from Seward, through Bear Mountain into Resurrection Bay. The contractor is to furnish all labor, equipment, supplies, materials, supervision, and other items and services necessary to accomplish the work. The contractor shall comply with commercial and industry standards as well as all applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, and procedures. Construction wage rates (formerly Davis-Bacon Act wage rates) shall apply. This includes providing comprehensive management, training, licensed personnel with facility access, tools, and labor necessary to perform all functions, operations, and tasks. Specific critical areas of the PWS are the routine inspection and monitoring of the facility infrastructure, including electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems. Maintaining the building automation systems (BAS) controls. Emergency response preparedness, such as backup power, fire protection system maintenance, chemical spills, water damage/leaks, and inclement weather. Without ongoing support for these functions, the risks to personnel health, government property, and ongoing research would be unacceptable. No other source can complete the in-progress tasks/services under the current orders and any other source would be required to begin the work again.
